source: part / whole * 100 percent

args.part: The part, for example operating income.
args.whole: The whole it is a part of, for example revenue. Not zero.

description: 100 * part / whole: the part (a profit, say) as a percent of the whole (the revenue). A zero whole is a division by zero fault, never a guess; negative values are used as given (a loss over positive revenue is a negative margin). Numbers in, so it works on any figures.
label: Margin: a part as a percent of a whole

source: (to - from) / abs(from) * 100 percent

description: 100 * (to - from) / abs(from): the change as a percent of the size of the starting figure. The absolute value keeps the sign meaningful when from is negative: a loss that shrinks from -50 to -25 is +50. A zero from is a division by zero fault.
label: Percent change from one figure to another

source: ((end / start) ^ (1 / years) - 1) * 100 percent

args.start: The starting figure. Not zero, same sign as end.
args.years: The number of years between them (may be fractional). Not zero.

description: 100 * ((end / start) ^ (1 / years) - 1): the constant yearly rate, as a percent, that takes start to end in years years. start and end must have the same sign and not be zero in start: a zero start or zero years is a division by zero fault, a negative ratio end / start is a domain fault. Years is a positive count (not checked; a negative one gives the reversed interval). Non-integer powers are the formula language's 34-digit POW-EXPLN.
label: Compound annual growth rate

source: part / total * 100 percent

description: 100 * part / total. The same arithmetic as margin, named for shares of a total (a segment of revenue, a line of the balance sheet). A zero total is a division by zero fault; a part larger than the total gives more than 100 and negative values are used as given.
label: A part as a percent of a total

source: year(at) - year(birth) - (if month(at) < month(birth) or (month(at) = month(birth) and day(at) < day(birth)) then 1 else 0)

args.birth: The date of birth (or the start date).

description: year(at) - year(birth), less 1 if the birthday (month and day) has not yet come in the year of at. A birthday on 29 February counts from 1 March in a year that has none. The completed years at the date; for an at before the birth the same rule gives a negative number, which is not an age.
label: Age in whole years at a date

source: to - from

description: to - from, in days (unit d): the number of calendar days after from that to falls; negative when to is earlier, zero for the same date. Calendar days, not business days, no day-count convention.
label: Days from one date to another

source: mesh-test.datumesh.com/sec/current_assets(cik: cik, fiscal_year: fiscal_year) / mesh-test.datumesh.com/sec/current_liabilities(cik: cik, fiscal_year: fiscal_year)

description: Current assets / current liabilities, both at the fiscal year's end, as reported (sec/current_assets over sec/current_liabilities). A year-end balance, not an average, as the ratio compares two balances of the same date. A zero liability is a division by zero fault; a company with no current assets tagged (a bank) has no value.

source: mesh-test.datumesh.com/sec/net_income(cik: cik, fiscal_year: fiscal_year) / ((mesh-test.datumesh.com/sec/total_assets(cik: cik, fiscal_year: fiscal_year) + mesh-test.datumesh.com/sec/total_assets(cik: cik, fiscal_year: fiscal_year - 1)) / 2) * 100 percent

The opening balance is the prior year's closing value from reported, so the first fiscal year in scope has no value. Percent. A zero average is a division by zero fault.

description: Average accounts payable / cost of revenue * 365 days: the average of the year-end accounts payable (sec/accounts_payable) and the prior fiscal year's, over cost of revenue of the fiscal year (sec/cost_of_revenue), times 365 (D37: average balance, 365 days).
